bytes.kicker: Travel · 10 listed hotel companies vs air
bytes.title: Hotels grew a median 14% while air travel shrank
bytes.dek: Rooms filled as flights thinned: IHCL's occupancy rose to 82% from 75% and Lemon Tree's RevPAR rose 18%, while ixigo's flight revenue fell 8% and TBO's air take rate slipped to about 2%.
bytes.read: Rooms are where Indian travel earns this season; watch whether air take rates stop falling over the winter schedule and Q3.

Chalet Hotels is left out because its reported revenue fell 32% on a year-ago residential handover (core revenue +11%), and EIH and Juniper had not filed. Margin is operating (EBITDA) margin vs Q2 FY26; 7 of 10 rose. Air figures are from the Q2 calls of Yatra (industry passengers and fares), ixigo and TBO Tek; ixigo also attributes part of its take-rate fall to discounts and a larger international mix.

bytes.dek: Textile exporters grew revenue a median 22% as US orders delayed by the 50% duty returned: Kitex, Indo Count and Pearl Global grew 37–66%, but Himatsingka and Trident shrank.
bytes.read: The US order recovery is real but uneven; watch whether exporters hold margins after the festive mix and whether UK and EU enquiries become orders.

bytes.kicker: Power equipment · transformer makers' Q2 FY27 margins
bytes.title: Transformer margins are splitting by voltage
bytes.dek: Makers of 400 kV-plus units widened EBITDA margins in Q2 (Kanohar to 35%, TARIL +6.2 pt). Makers of lower-voltage units gave margin back as copper and steel costs went only partly to buyers.
bytes.read: Pricing power now sits at 400 kV and above; the test is whether new capacity and slower awards spread the squeeze upward.

bytes.read: Cheaper parcels are reaching the platform's margin first; the Q3 festive print will show whether Meesho keeps ≈6% or hands it back in price.

bytes.kicker: Guidance direction · 1,128 Q2 FY27 calls read
bytes.title: Lenders guide up. Chemicals and FMCG guide down.
bytes.dek: Across 1,128 calls, 44% of managements cut or guided lower and 34% raised or guided higher. The split runs by sector, not by market.
bytes.read: Guidance is splitting by sector: lenders and auto makers sound confident, while chemicals, FMCG and IT are lowering the bar for H2.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of 1,128 Q2 FY27 earnings calls (BSE filings), as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: How it is counted: a call counts as raising when management raised a number it had guided before, or gave guidance that reads as positive; it counts as cutting when it cut a guided number or gave guidance that reads as negative. A call can count on both sides. Net = % raising − % cutting, per sector, for sectors with at least 25 Q2 FY27 calls read. Open Sectors → Guidance leaders for the companies behind each bar.

bytes.kicker: Aerospace & defence · 26 companies reported Q2 FY27
bytes.title: Defence revenue grew 42%. Private suppliers led.
bytes.dek: Order books are turning into revenue: the median defence company grew sales 42% year on year, and defence indigenisation came up on 93 Q2 calls, up from 80 two quarters ago.
bytes.read: The defence order cycle is now visible in revenue, and the smaller private suppliers of electronics, drones and components are converting it fastest.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026; theme counts from Vantage call tracker

bytes.kicker: Data-centre power & cooling · 110 Q2 FY27 calls
bytes.title: Everyone is talking data centres. The numbers aren't showing it yet.
bytes.dek: In capital goods, companies that discussed data centres grew revenue 27.8%, about the same as peers that didn't (27.4%).
bytes.read: Data-centre demand is real for a few suppliers, but as a theme it is crowded: mentioning it on a call has not yet meant faster growth than peers.
bytes.sources: Vantage theme tracker and Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE, as of 18 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: A call counts when management discusses data-centre power, cooling, cables or electrical equipment demand. The comparison uses capital goods companies whose Q2 FY27 calls Vantage read, split by whether the call discussed the theme. Mentions say nothing about how big data centres are in each company's revenue.

bytes.kicker: Autos · 55 component makers, 5 tyre makers, 5 two-wheeler makers
bytes.title: Auto parts grew 32%. Margins went the other way.
bytes.dek: Component makers grew revenue a median 32%, but the median operating margin slipped 0.5 points.
bytes.read: Volumes are not the question in autos this season; margins are. Recovery in H2 depends on passing higher costs through to customers.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE (consolidated where available), as of 18 Nov 2026
